I give up. I did not change `/work/putnam_2021_a6.lean`, so the `sorry` is still there.

The easy parts are straightforward. Since `P` is a product of nonconstant integer polynomials, it is nonzero, so `P(2) ≥ 1`. `P(2) = 1` would force `P = 1`, which is constant, a contradiction. That gives `P(2) ≠ 0` and `P(2) ≠ 1`.

The hard part is showing `P(2)` is not prime. The known argument is a genuine olympiad-level analysis of the factors of a 0/1-coefficient polynomial, and I do not have a complete argument I could formalize. Mathlib also lacks convenient tools for root location and bounds of that kind. Producing a verified Lean proof would need a substantial development that I cannot complete here.
